item.title: Some new criteria for the uniqueness of limit cycles in Rayleigh--Lienard systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.33114v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, new uniqueness criteria for Rayleigh--Li\'enard systems with damping of positive odd degree in the velocity are established. Under suitable conditions, any limit cycle is unique and hyperbolic, with its stability determined by the damping signs. Neither symmetry nor monotonicity of the damping and restoring functions is required. Changes of variables and time yield further criteria for generalized Kukles systems. Applications to three polynomial families yield uniqueness and nonexistence results. In particular, we resolve an open uniqueness problem for a hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator left open by Chen et al. (Phys. D, 2021). We also give an alternative uniqueness proof for a system with homogeneous components and obtain uniqueness and nonexistence results for a modified hybrid van der Pol--Rayleigh oscillator.
item.dc:creator: Hebai Chen, Dongmei Xiao, Rui Zhang

item.title: Flocking with finite communication speed: a Doppler-inspired Lyapunov approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.33170v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Cucker--Smale model with state-dependent transmission delays arising from finite-speed information propagation. Our main contribution is a Lyapunov functional inspired by the Doppler effect, combining a delay potential with a logarithmic correction involving the receiver velocity. Its dissipation yields uniform delay bounds without relying on velocity contraction estimates. For two agents in one spatial dimension, we prove asymptotic flocking for arbitrary compatible subluminal initial histories, assuming only that the influence function has a divergent integral at infinity. A bounded geometric correction extends this result to arbitrary spatial dimension when all values of the initial velocity histories lie on one common affine line. For multiple agents in one dimension, we obtain uniform delay bounds, and thus flocking, provided that a fixed agent is leftmost for all sufficiently large times. In all these flocking regimes, the spatial diameter remains uniformly bounded and the velocity diameter decays exponentially. We also derive a conditional criterion involving logarithmic sums when the leftmost agent changes infinitely often. Finally, we construct a multidimensional analogue of the Doppler-inspired functional and identify an additional assumption needed to obtain delay bounds in the general case.
item.dc:creator: Jan Haskovec, Mauro Rodriguez Cartabia

item.title: Maximizing Measures for Subadditive and Almost-Additive Potentials on Countable-Alphabet Subshifts
item.description: arXiv:2610.33218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of maximizing measures for subadditive and almost-additive families of upper semicontinuous, bounded-above potentials $\mathcal F=\{f_n\}_{n\geq1}$ on closed subshifts over countable alphabets. Under a coercivity condition on $f_1$, we prove that every maximizing sequence, that is, $\{\mu_k\}_{k\geq1}\subset\mathcal M_\sigma(X)$ satisfying $\bar{\mathcal F}(\mu_k)\to\beta(\mathcal F)$, is uniformly tight, preventing mass from escaping to arbitrarily large symbols. As a consequence, a maximizing measure exists.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Freire, Juliano S. Gonschorowski

item.title: Some remarks on polynomial vector fields in $\RR^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study planar polynomial vector fields admitting invariant circles. We characterize polynomial vector fields having $m$ concentric invariant circles, and we describe those having three invariant circles whose centers are not collinear. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for the unit circle to be the unique limit cycle of a quadratic vector field. We prove that a cubic or quartic Kolmogorov vector field having the unit circle invariant has no circular limit cycle, and that a quartic vector field with two concentric circular limit cycles has at most three circular limit cycles, this bound being sharp.
item.dc:creator: Supriyo Jana, Soumen Sarkar

item.title: On the stability of rank-one factors for Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.33228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove $C^1$-stability of $C^\infty$ rank-one factors for a large class of higher rank Anosov $\mathbb Z^k$-actions. If the factor is a projection of a smooth fiber bundle and the action contains an element which acts as the identity on the rank-one factor and is Anosov on every fiber, then any sufficiently $C^1$-small $C^\infty$ perturbation of the action will also have a $C^\infty$ rank-one factor. In particular, we prove the $C^1$-stability of the product structure for Anosov $\mathbb Z^2$-actions which are obtained as a (diagonal) product of two $\mathbb Z$-Anosov actions.
item.dc:creator: Danijela Damjanovic, Jiesong Zhang

item.title: Gibbs measures on Cayley trees and homoclinic orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.33287v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the question of existence and multiplicity of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures on Cayley trees with spin space $\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that, under a natural summability assumption on the interaction function, there are always at least two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying two natural symmetry conditions. Moreover, any two homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures satisfying a suitable non-degeneracy assumption can be superimposed and produce infinitely many other homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures. When the interaction function $Q$ has bounded support in $\mathbb{Z}$, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a symplectomorphism of $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$, where $n$ is the smallest natural number such that $Q(i)=0$ for every $i>n$. For $n=1$, results from symbolic dynamics and horseshoes imply the existence of homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures whose single-site marginal is concentrated near an arbitrary finite subset of $N\mathbb{Z}$, where $N$ is a sufficiently large integer. In the case of interaction functions with infinite support, there is a one-to-one correspondence between homogeneous Markov Gibbs measures and suitable homoclinic orbits of a Lagrangian correspondence on the cotangent bundle of a Banach space.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Abbondandolo, Pietro Majer

item.title: The Intersection of nested filled-in little Julia sets have zero area
item.description: arXiv:2610.33328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is shown that for any infinitely renormalizable quadratic polynomial $Q_c$ the intersection $K_\infty$ of all the little filled-in Julia sets (renormalization Julia sets) containing the critical value have zero area.
item.dc:creator: Carsten Lunde Petersen

item.title: Ambient Chain-Relation Reduction in Contracting Controlled Skew-Product Semiflows
item.description: arXiv:2610.33519v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The qualitative dynamics of nonautonomous differential equations is often studied through cocycles and skew-product semiflows over a driving base. We develop a chain-recurrence reduction principle for systems admitting an equivariant attracting section and uniform asymptotic tracking. The abstract theorem determines the complete chain-attainability relation in the ambient phase space: chains may start off the attracting section, but every attainable target lies on it and is selected solely by the factor semiflow. Applied to contracting controlled skew-product semiflows, this gives exact descriptions of the chain recurrent set, chain components, Conley order, compact strictly invariant sets, attractors, basins, and dual repellers. A weighted-supremum transverse gauge yields a complete Lyapunov function for the full semiflow while preserving the recurrent values of the base. The differential hypotheses are verified through subadditive fiber-derivative growth and averaged moving-metric logarithmic norms, allowing transient expansion and non-unique ergodicity. Quantitative persistence is established for finite-window maps and smooth vector-field perturbations. The results provide a unified framework for chain recurrence, Lyapunov structure, and attractor--repeller geometry in contracting nonautonomous dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Robert Vrabel

item.title: A structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems
item.description: arXiv:2610.33596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, the author refuted several conjectures about the vanishing of multiple correlation sequences. The goal of this paper is to provide a counterpart for the conjectures of Frantzikinakis--Kuca and of Leibman. The significance of this manuscript is twofold: firstly, we provide a structure theorem for multiple correlation sequences on nilsystems along arithmetic progressions (in the sense of Frantzikinakis--Kuca), and a corresponding structure theorem for polynomial orbits of subnilmanifolds in connected nilmanifolds (in the sense of Leibman). Secondly, we identify null generalized nilsequences, as a notion of smallness, which provides a structured counterpart for null sequences. In particular, in the special case of ergodic nilsystems, we answer positively a question of Frantzikinakis on the structure of multiple correlation sequences.
item.dc:creator: Or Shalom

item.title: Zeros of Melnikov functions for periodically perturbed Hamiltonian systems with random coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2610.33620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Introducing a probabilistic perspective on a classical theme within the study of chaotic dynamics, we investigate the zeros of the Melnikov distance function associated to a periodically perturbed Hamiltonian system when the perturbation has random coefficients. We provide asymptotic estimates (as the period of the perturbation becomes large or small) for the average number of zeros and for the probability of no zeros.
item.dc:creator: Ali Ittayem, Erik Lundberg

item.title: Weak mixing and non-recurrence along finitely generated multiplicative semigroups of $\mathbb N$
item.description: arXiv:2610.33710v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal P$ be a finite nonempty set of primes, and let $S_{\mathcal P}$ be the multiplicative semigroup that they generate. We prove that there are an invertible weakly mixing measure-preserving transformation $T$ and a set $A$ of positive measure such that $A\cap T^{-r}A=\varnothing$ for every $r\in S_{\mathcal P}$. This gives a negative answer to Bergelson's 1996 question concerning recurrence along $\{2^m3^n:m,n\geq1\}$, and applies to every finitely generated multiplicative semigroup of positive integers. More generally, we give a sufficient condition for weakly mixing non-recurrence based on divisibility properties and separation by finitely many rotations of the circle. This criterion also applies to an infinitely generated multiplicative semigroup not contained in any $S_{\mathcal P}$ with $\mathcal P$ finite.
item.dc:creator: Zhuowei Liu

item.title: Magnetic billiards:duality and magnetic Radon property
item.description: arXiv:2610.33782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Birkhoff magnetic billiards inside convex planar domains for a constant weak magnetic field. We prove that there exists a functional family of centrally-symmetric convex billiard tables satisfying the so-called magnetic Radon property. These are tables which have a rotational invariant curves consisting of $4$-periodic orbits with the rotation numbers either $1/4$ or $3/4$. These billiard tables can be constructed in a neighborhood of circles. However in our construction we do not use perturbation methods but rather some topological argument for the system of ODEs governing the magnetic Radon property. In contrast with this result we consider the magnetic billiard tables having discrete rotational symmetry for the angle $2\pi/k, k\in\mathbb{Z}$. We prove that in this case a rotational invariant curve consisting of $k$-periodic orbits exists, if and only if the billiard table is circular. We develop several tools, which, we believe, are important for other aspects of magnetic billiards. The first is the "magnetic duality" which enables to work with the dual object---the outer magnetic billiard. Secondly, we find the generating functions of outer magnetic billiard, both the ''standard" and the "non-standard" ones.
item.dc:creator: Michael (Misha), Bialy

item.title: Stationary Random Iterations of Lipschitz Maps: A Generalized Displacement Condition for the Existence of Invariant Structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.33829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study random iterations generated by infinitely many Lipschitz maps on non-compact complete separable metric spaces. We generalize classical displacement conditions ensuring the existence and uniqueness of invariant structures. We prove two main results. The first uses the graph transform operator to extend Elton's condition [A multiplicative ergodic theorem for Lipschitz maps. Stochastic Process. Appl. 34(1) (1990)] for the existence and uniqueness of invariant graphs. The second uses the Markov operator to generalize a displacement condition for stationary measures, introduced by Diaconis and Freedman [Iterated random functions. SIAM Rev. 41(1) (1999)] and by Kloeckner [Optimal transportation and stationary measures for iterated function systems. Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 173(1) (2022)]. We present several examples illustrating the applicability of our results.
item.dc:creator: Bella Figliaggi, Edgar Matias, Tiago Pereira

item.title: On tame amenable flows and generalized Newelski's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.33830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We are developing some topological dynamics below a given ambit. We define and study Bohr compactifications below ambits and other related objects. We describe a natural epimorphism from the Ellis group of an ambit to the Bohr compactification below its Ellis semigroup ambit. The first main result says that, assuming tameness and hereditary amenability, this natural map is an isomorphism of topological groups. This is an abstract dynamical generalization of Newelski's conjecture, or rather a theorem of Chernikov and Simon that a natural map from the Ellis group of the flow $(S_G(M),G)$ to the definable Bohr compactification of $G$ is an isomorphism when $G$ is a definably amenable group definable in a NIP structure $M$. We give two proofs of our main result: a shorter dynamical proof and an analytic proof. In the course of the dynamical proof, we prove some results on the universal compactification flow and on the generalized Bohr compactification below a given ambit which admits a left continuous semigroup operation extending the action of $G$. The considerations around the analytic proof yield a description of the measured structure of amenable tame minimal flows, which is the second main result of this paper. We also study specializations of the above abstract topological dynamics context to model theory contexts to recover some known and to obtain some new notions and results. The main new results in the model theory contexts are: (i) a description of the Bohr compactification of the group of automorphisms of a sufficiently saturated model $\mathfrak{C}$ of a first order theory $T$ below a certain fundamental ambit associated with $\mathfrak{C}$; (ii) transfer of amenability of a NIP theory $T$ to amenability of the Ellis semigroup ambit; (iii) a version of Newelski's conjecture for spaces of local types with a description of Bohr compactifications below such spaces.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Max Hoffmann, Krzysztof Krupi\'nski

item.title: Thermodynamic formalism for partially hyperbolic endomorphisms with critical set
item.description: arXiv:2610.34068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the thermodynamic formalism of a broad class of partially hyperbolic, non-uniformly expanding endomorphisms with critical set, and show that they admit unique equilibrium states for all H\"older potentials of small variation. In particular, our results yield uniqueness of equilibrium states for Viana maps with small variation H\"older potentials, for non-uniformly expanding interval maps with finitely many critical points and hyperbolic H\"older potentials, and for Benedicks-Carleson quadratic maps with arbitrary H\"older potentials.
item.dc:creator: Kecheng Li

item.title: Hausdorff and Packing Measures for $\beta$-L{\"u}roth Infinite Iterated Function Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.34076v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Hausdorff and packing measures of attractors generated by infinite $\beta$-L\"uroth iterated function systems. Let $I\subset\mathbb N$ be infinite and let $\dim_H E_I=h$. For a regular system, we first give conditions for the positivity of $\mathcal H^h(E_I)$ and the finiteness of $\mathcal P^h(E_I)$ in terms of first-level L\"uroth intervals. We then introduce tail-regular partitions and the scale $R_n=\frac{B_n^\infty}{B_n}.$ Under tail-regularity, the Hausdorff and packing conditions reduce to counting conditions for $I$ on intervals of length comparable to $R_n$, together with a tail condition in the packing case. Finally, we apply these results to regularly varying partitions and stretched-exponential partitions.
item.dc:creator: Junjue Miao, Tianrui Wang

item.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions II: quadratic differential equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34201v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate differential equations defined through elements of a nonassociative five-dimensional real algebra $\mathcal A_\gamma$, and show that every system of quadratic differential equations $\dot p=F(p)$ on $\mathbb R^5$ can be written as a differential equation over such a non-flexible quadratic algebra. We then study quadratic differential equations and their solutions over the whole family $\{\mathcal A_\gamma\}_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}$ of algebras while varying $\gamma$ across the parameter interval $[0,1]$, exploiting the fact that by definition, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra and that $\mathcal A_1=\mathbb{P}$ is the real Pentarnion algebra. We construct explicit Jacobi elliptic solutions that deform a quaternion-valued solution at $\gamma=0$ into a Pentarnion-valued one at $\gamma=1$, and an algebra-valued Riccati equation whose equilibrium $p=0$ loses stability at a critical value of $\gamma$. Numerical experiments indicate period doubling, coexisting stable periodic orbits and irregular dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Poshtkohi, Susanne Pumpluen

item.title: A Five-Dimensional Nonassociative Algebra: elliptic integrability and bracketing-dependent dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.34202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a five-dimensional nonassociative real algebra $\mathbb{P}$ whose one-generated subalgebras are complex while its left, middle, and right nuclei are all $\mathbb{R}$. This contrast permits an unambiguous one-element functional calculus but makes polynomial ordinary differential equations sensitive to bracketing. We classify the homogeneous quadratic words containing one fixed coefficient $B$ and two copies of $p$ that preserve $\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\{1,B,p\}$. For a fixed-coefficient family of Pentarnion ODEs interpolating between $B(pp)$ and $(Bp)p$, changing only the bracketing preserves the linearisation but changes the observed global dynamics. Exact balance identities isolate the associator contribution, while numerical diagnostics support bounded chaos at one endpoint and an attracting periodic orbit at the other. The flexibility defect $p(Bp)-(pB)p=-[p,B,p]$ also produces a rank jump: after polarisation, one-generated subalgebras have dimension three on a nonempty Zariski-open set, rather than at most two. On a canonical invariant three-dimensional space the resulting flow has two first integrals and an explicit periodic orbit on an elliptic curve. We also construct a dense five-dimensional quadratic flow with a full-affine-span Jacobi-elliptic solution. Its projective closure is an elliptic normal sextic, and representation by two ordered products selects the modulus $m=1/2$.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Poshtkohi, Susanne Pumpluen

item.title: Finiteness of ergodic measures of maximal entropy for certain skew product systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.34209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consider a $C^{1+\beta}$ skew product $F$ over a topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphism $f$, with fiber dynamics driven by a $C^{1+\beta}$ $\mathbb{R}^k$-action $\{\rho_{\bf t}\}$ on a closed manifold $Y$ through a $C^{1+\beta}$ cocycle $\tau$. Suppose that the fiber action preserves an ergodic smooth measure of maximal entropy $m_{\operatorname{MME}}$. Under a nondegeneracy condition called joint nontriviality, and assuming that each element $\rho_{\bf t}$ is either of class $C^\infty$ or hyperbolic, we prove that $F$ admits only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy. Moreover, every such measure is of the form $\mu\times m_{\operatorname{MME}}$, where $\mu$ is an ergodic equilibrium state for a H\"older potential on the base. If, in addition, the fiber action is exponentially mixing of all orders, then every ergodic MME is Bernoulli, exponentially mixing of all orders, and satisfies the Central Limit Theorem. Our main novelties are entropy formulas for skew products, obtained through the cone property and $r$-neutralized entropy, and a relative Ledrappier--Young theorem that converts the fiber entropy contribution into absolute continuity of fiberwise conditional measures. Combined with nonlinear thermodynamic formalism, rotation theory and Yomdin theory, these yield the finiteness of the base projections and the product rigidity of ergodic MMEs.
item.dc:creator: Changguang Dong, Qiujie Qiao

item.title: Quasicircularity of the Zakeri Curve and Capture Component Boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2610.34225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a fixed irrational rotation number of bounded type, we prove that the locus of critically marked cubic polynomials whose two critical points lie on the boundary of the fixed Siegel disk is a quasicircle. This locus is known as the Zakeri curve. The main step is a boundary correspondence lemma for holomorphic families of disks with uniformly quasiconformal extensions. We further prove that every capture component in this family is a quasidisk, including components attached to the Zakeri curve.
item.dc:creator: Yuming Fu, Weiwei Su

item.title: Bistable fronts in periodic media: phase reduction and realization of circle flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.34228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a phase reduction and a converse realization theorem for front dynamics in one-dimensional periodic reaction-diffusion-advection equations. For sufficiently large periods under local bistability, and sufficiently small periods when the homogenized equation admits a stationary front, we construct strictly ordered invariant front families that are normally exponentially attracting and locally complete for entire orbits. Modulo spatial-period translations, the dynamics on each family reduces exactly to a circle flow: rotations correspond to propagating pulsating fronts, equilibria to stationary fronts, and connecting orbits to transition fronts between stationary fronts. Conversely, every smooth circle flow can be realized, up to time-preserving topological conjugacy, as the quotient dynamics of such a family for a periodic, locally bistable equation with constant diffusion and no advection. Realizations with a Cantor set of stationary phases and a connecting orbit in each complementary interval illustrate the richness of front dynamics in these media. We also obtain first-order phase-velocity expansions in both period limits, quantitative propagation laws near zero frozen speed, and global exponential orbital stability of propagating pulsating fronts.
item.dc:creator: Weiwei Ding, Xing Liang, Linfeng Xu

item.title: Temporal central limit theorem for mixed-radix odometer discrepancy
item.description: arXiv:2610.34243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the local discrepancy for the number of visits of the orbit of $0$ under a mixed-radix odometer to intervals near the origin. Both the length of the orbit and the endpoint of the visited interval are chosen independently and uniformly at random. Under a Feller-type condition and an explicit condition ensuring that the finite random-time clock can be approximated by a Haar clock on the fluctuation scale, we obtain a temporal central limit theorem for the discrepancy, with an explicit Kolmogorov-Smirnov rate of convergence. This extends and strengthens the fixed-base temporal central limit theorem of Levin and Merzbach to the mixed-radix setting.
item.dc:creator: Maria Avdeeva, Francesco Cellarosi

item.title: Network of limit sets in dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.34265v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Points within a topological dynamical systems can be separated into transient and recurrent points. Most of the asymptotic properties of the dynamics is borne by the closure of the collection of recurrent points. This article presents a representation scheme for dynamics using the connectivity information in terms of the recurrent set. This representation is functorial and represents certain compositional features of dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Suddhasattwa Das

item.title: Pointwise ergodic theorems along oscillating sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.34301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the first pointwise convergence result for nonconventional ergodic averages modeled along a large class of oscillating sequences, treating, for example, orbits of the form $\big(\lfloor n^d\sin(e\pi n)\rfloor\big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$, $d\in\mathbb{N}$. More specifically, for every probability space $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ equipped with an invertible measure-preserving transformation $T\colon X\to X$ and every $f\in L^p_{\mu}(X)$ with $p\in(1,\infty]$, we prove that the limit \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^Nf\big(T^{\lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor}x\big)\quad\text{exists for $\mu$-a.e. $x\in X$,} \] where $P$ is a non-constant polynomial with real coefficients, $\psi$ is $1$-periodic and real-analytic, and $\alpha$ has irrationality exponent smaller than $1+\sqrt{\operatorname{deg}(P)+1}$. On the one hand, the latter assumption is satisfied by a.e. $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$, and, on the other hand, our result covers any of the following concrete orbits \[ \lfloor n\cos(e\pi n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\lfloor n^{37}\sin(n)\rfloor\text{,}\quad\big\lfloor \sqrt{2}n^{10}e^{\sin(\pi (\sqrt[5]{7}+1) n)}\big\rfloor\text{,}\quad \big\lfloor \big((\log 2) n^3+e n\big)e^{e^{\cos(\pi \sqrt{2} n)}}\big\rfloor\text{.} \] The proof employs the so-called one-frequency circle method for estimating exponential sums with phases $\big(\xi \lfloor P(n)\psi(\alpha n)\rfloor\big)_{1\le n\le N}$, but the major arc approximants of our exponential sums do not consist of their direct continuous counterparts. In the major arc regime we decouple the $\psi$-oscillatory part of the phase from the polynomial one, and approximate the exponential sum by $\int_0^1\big(\frac{1}{N}\int_0^Ne^{2\pi i\xi P(t)\psi( s)}dt\big)ds$. This represents a novel phenomenon for problems of this kind, and, interestingly, our proof exploits the coefficient-free variational estimates of Radon-type operators.
item.dc:creator: Leonidas Daskalakis

item.title: Constellations for Lyapunov exponents
item.description: arXiv:2610.34306v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the maximal Lyapunov exponent of random products of positive matrices, and prove that it can be calculated to arbitrary precision with arithmetic work polynomial in the number of requested digits. In nondegenerate settings, the complexity of our method depends on the intrinsic complexity of the dynamics---which we characterize---and not on the Euclidean dimension of the ambient space in which the dynamics live. As numerical applications, we determine the Hausdorff dimension of random intersections of Sierpi\'nski gaskets, and Viswanath's constant---the growth rate of the random Fibonacci sequence. We first establish a general inequality for nonnegative matrix families showing that, if a signed measure with finite support is sufficiently close to being stationary, then it predicts the Lyapunov exponent accurately. This framework also encompasses Pollicott's Fredholm determinant approximation. We then show that, just like drawing a constellation by picking bright stars, one can construct a sequence of signed measures approximating stationarity by picking informative orbits of the projective dynamics. Furthermore, we prove that our construction uses an asymptotically optimal number of atoms, which is governed by an intrinsic quantity we call constellation dimension.
item.dc:creator: Nima Alibabaei

item.title: Variational principle for the Carath\'eodory--Pesin entropy of foliations
item.description: arXiv:2610.34557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce Carath\'eodory-Pesin structures for non-singular foliations on Riemannian manifolds and define a new notion of entropy for such foliations. Under dynamical and geometric assumptions on the corresponding holonomy pseudogroups, we establish a variational description of this new concept which relates it to the local metric entropy of measures on transversals and to the entropy of harmonic measures on the manifold.
item.dc:creator: Andrzej Bi\'s, Maria Carvalho, Paulo Varandas

item.title: Quantitative Persistence and Regularity of Invariant Graphs for Dissipative Twist Maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.35068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the robustness of invariant Lagrangian graphs for dissipative twist maps on $\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$ in the $C^r$ category, for any $r\ge 1$, and show their persistence as invariant global attractors under quantitative sharp conditions involving both the size of dissipation parameter and the perturbation at stake. Note that when $d>1$ the geometric Lagrangian property of the invariant manifold may be destroyed, so that the graph may persist but fail to be Lagrangian. In general, additional dynamical requirements on the twist maps come into play if we intend to preserve also the Lagrangian property. In this line, we first study their persistence for general perturbations, then we restrict to the class of exact conformally symplectic twist maps and provide quantitative sharp conditions for the persistence of invariant exact Lagrangian graphs, without assuming any condition on the tangential dynamics of the manifold. The persistence result relies on a combination of a suitable multidimensional Herman--Mather formula proved in this setting and contraction estimates that provide sharp bounds on the $C^1$-norm of the perturbation to get a unique, globally attracting $C^r$ graph. In dimension $d=1$, by further assuming that that the circle map induced by the graph has irrational rotation number, we prove that every $C^1$ invariant graph of a $C^k$ map is $C^k$ for $k=2,3,\ldots,\infty$. Analytic maps with Lipschitz, non-$C^1$ invariant graphs at every prescribed irrational rotation number show that this initial regularity assumption is essential.
item.dc:creator: Deyu Kong, Jessica Elisa Massetti, Lin Wang

item.title: Large deviations for observables with logarithmic singularity and differentiability of the pressure function
item.description: arXiv:2610.35221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that logarithmic observables of form $\phi(x)=\log(|x-b|)$ on the doubling map $T$ have exponential large deviations with respect to the invariant measure if $b$ is preperiodic but not periodic with respect to $T$ giving a counterpart to the known result of strictly stretched exponential large deviations in the case that $b$ is periodic. These results are established by showing that the topological pressure function developed for unbounded observables is differentiable at $0$.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Nicol, Tanja I. Schindler

item.title: A non-perturbative topological persistence theorem for normally hyperbolic invariant manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.35258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Floer proved that, under a sufficiently small $C^0$ perturbation, a normally hyperbolic invariant manifold gives rise to a nearby invariant set whose cohomology ring contains a subring isomorphic to that of the original manifold. Using topological conditions, expressed in terms of the so-called covering relations, we generalize this theorem to a non-perturbative context. Our result does not require the existence of an invariant manifold before perturbation, nor does it require the original map to be smooth or invertible. For the proof, we develop an additional structure on the Conley index for maps on vector bundles.
item.dc:creator: Wojciech Sp\'olnik, Maciej J. Capi\'nski

item.title: Influence of Anthropisation on a Mosquito Community in a Tropical Forest-Village Interface
item.description: arXiv:2610.35435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tropical forests are undergoing deep changes caused by human activities, which have repercussions on the habitats of wild animal, particularly mammals. As mammals serve as a main source of blood meals for forest mosquitoes, their decline may affect the mosquitoes, as do changes in their habitats and abiotic conditions, such as rainfall, temperature, etc. Finally, along with humans come new species of mosquitoes-more generalist and more anthropophilic-that adapt to these new conditions and, moreover, serve as vectors for re-emerging diseases against which local populations have no more immunity. In this work, we derive a deterministic model which includes the effects of anthropisation, two species of mosquito that interact with one another (one is a generalist, whilst the other is sedentary and lives in the forest), and blood feeding preferences between multiple blood sources. We consider two socio-ecological areas, corresponding to a domestic area (for instance, a village), and a wild area (for instance, a tropical forest). A comprehensive analysis of the system is carried out using classical theory and monotone systems theory. We analyse the efficiency of individual protective measures, such as mosquito nets and repellents, against the domestic mosquito species. We investigate the risk of invasion of the wild area by a generalist mosquito species. We show that habitat anthropisation and high interspecific competition facilitate the invasion. When the mathematical system converges towards a periodic cycle, we provide numerical estimates for the periodic invasion threshold. Using a global sensitivity analysis, we show that the model is sensitive to the level of anthropisation, the adaptability of the invasive species to the forest area, and its fitness. The more efficient way to control the invasion is, therefore, to limit, as much as possible, the forest anthropisation.
item.dc:creator: Dumont Yves, H\'etier Marc, Yatat-Djeumen Valaire

item.title: The Formal Critical Coupling of the Four-Dimensional Anderson Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.35459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we present a formal renormalization-group (RG) calculation for the weakly coupled four-dimensional elliptic Anderson model. Under a scale-independent bare-coupling convention, and with the normalization $\lambda_{\varepsilon}$, the bubble-chain resummation yields the geometric series $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(\lambda)$, with a formal pole at $\lambda_c$. We stress that this pole is a feature of the formal bare bubble series. The argument combines Bogoliubov-Parasiuk-Hepp-Zimmermann (BPHZ) renormalization, a Hepp-sector motivated restriction to the bubble-chain subclass for explicit resummation, and an explicit summation of the resulting geometric series. Numerically, we illustrate the analytic building blocks of the formal expansion: the massive Green function, the bubble integral, the geometric resummation, the extraction of the formal pole from synthetic noisy data, a kurtosis diagnostic, and a phase diagram of the formal variance. These computations visualize the deterministic kernels and the formal resummation used above. Using spectral methods and nonlinear least-squares fitting, we verify the short-distance asymptotic behaviour of the massive Green function for $G=(1-\Delta)^{-1}\delta_0$, reproduce the logarithmic divergence of the bubble integral in four dimensions, compute the formal effective variance $\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{formal}}(\lambda)$ arising from the bubble-chain resummation, locate the formal pole at $\lambda_c$, and draw a schematic phase diagram of the formal variance in the $(\lambda,\log\varepsilon)$ plane. The kurtosis diagnostic uses a synthetic proxy for the non-Gaussian regime; the sharp change is imposed by construction. Nonlinear fitting of synthetic data recovers the formal pole within the statistical uncertainty of the synthetic noise. Our results illustrate the analytic formulas and the fitting procedure.
item.dc:creator: Shenglan Yuan

item.title: Periodic data conjugacy for diffeomorphism cocycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.35460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider H\"older continuous cocycles over a hyperbolic dynamical system with values in the group of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold. We focus on establishing conjugacy between two cocycles from conjugacy of their periodic data. We obtain such a result under bunching, or domination, assumption on the cocycles and a mild regularity assumption in $C^0$ topology on the maps conjugating the periodic data. We also obtain conjugacy to a constant cocycle assuming boundedness in $C^1$ or pre-compactness in $C^0$ for the constant cocycle and the conjugating maps.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Sadovskaya

item.title: Graph-Convolutional Reinforcement Learning for Finite-Time Stabilization of a Chaotic Chua Circuit via Unified Flexible Terminal Sliding-Mode Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.35613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a graph convolutional reinforcement learning framework for the finite-time stabilization of chaotic dynamics in a physical Chua circuit. The circuit is modeled directly in terms of capacitor voltages, inductor current, and physical component parameters. This preserves the connection between the mathematical model and the underlying electrical system. A unified, flexible terminal sliding-mode controller is developed to achieve stabilization within a finite time in the presence of uncertainties in the lumped model, external disturbances, and bounded control inputs. The controller incorporates state-dependent nonlinear exponents to provide flexible convergence characteristics while avoiding singular terms near equilibrium. To minimize dependence on manual controller tuning, the admissible controller parameters are optimized using an actor-critic reinforcement learning scheme with a graph convolutional network that leverages the circuit dynamics' coupling structure. The learned parameters are constrained to the ranges required by the theoretical stability conditions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the rapid suppression of chaotic oscillations and the finite-time convergence of the state and sliding variables while respecting the prescribed input-saturation limits. Compared to a reference control method, the proposed approach reduces the IAE, ISE, ITAE, and ITSE by 56.27\,\%, 56.40\,\%, 61.69\,\%, and 64.70\,\%, respectively. These results suggest that graph-based reinforcement learning can effectively tune parameters while retaining the robustness and analytical structure of the underlying sliding-mode controller.
item.dc:creator: Hooman Fatoorehchi, Majid Roohi, Rasmus Kold, Matthias Ehrhardt, Andreas Basse-O'Connor, Sebastian Nis Bay Villadsen, Philip L. Fosb{\o}l

item.title: Local Koopman modes of saddle-point diffusions: exact singular functions and a data-driven estimator
item.description: arXiv:2610.35627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherent sets-regions of phase space that resist mixing-organize transport in stochastic dynamical systems and are encoded in the leading singular functions of the stochastic Koopman operator. These are typically computed numerically and globally; a local, analytic theory near a fixed point has been missing, although fixed points and the transitions between them organize the flow. We supply the local theory for a saddle, the transition state through which probability flows between basins. Naively the construction fails-probability escapes along unstable directions, the invariant measure is non-normalizable, the singular functions leave $L^2$, and singular values exceed one. We show that conditioning on non-escape (a Doob's $h$-transform) repairs this; that the required $h$ is the unique stabilizing solution of an algebraic Riccati equation; and that the resulting slow modes decay at the escape rate along the unstable manifold. We obtain these modes in closed form-products of Hermite polynomials in canonical coordinates times the $h$-function-and use their unitary structure to derive a data-driven estimator: canonical correlation analysis on conditioned trajectories. When a single unstable direction dominates, the leading mode is the reaction coordinate, locally recovering the stable manifold and committor of transition-path theory. The construction connects coherent sets to transition-path theory, to the stabilizing Riccati solution of linear control, and to the time-reversed dynamics of generative diffusion models.
item.dc:creator: Xuehao Ding

item.title: Isomorphisms of $\ell^1$-crossed products of topological systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.33050v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a complete description of the isometric isomorphisms between the $\ell^1$-crossed products of actions of discrete groups on nonempty compact Hausdorff spaces. In particular, two such crossed products are isometrically isomorphic as Banach algebras if and only if the actions are topologically isomorphic. It follows that $\ell^1(G\curvearrowright X)$ remembers not just $X$ but even the acting group and the action, and is not determined by the transformation groupoid $G\ltimes X$ alone. The proof recovers $C(X)$ from the hermitian elements and uses the geometry of $L^p$-spaces to identify the invertible isometries. We also obtain analogous results for measurable actions.
item.dc:creator: Eusebio Gardella, Tabar\'e Roland

item.title: Locally eventually onto cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.33131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new checkable criterion to ensure that a one-dimensional cellular automaton on a finite alphabet is locally eventually onto. In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention. Building on Sutner's work with de Bruijn graphs, we describe a method for deciding openness and at the same time determining n. We then introduce the notion of block-regularity of local rules as a generalization of bipermutivity and prove that it implies openness. We further identify two conditions that, together with block-regularity, ensure that every nonempty cylinder set is mapped onto the whole configuration space after a finite number of iterations, and hence that the cellular automaton is locally eventually onto. The appendix provides the algorithms that check these finite criteria and then presents examples of locally eventually onto, non-bipermutive cellular automata for small diameters.
item.dc:creator: Jan Kristian Haugland, Nadia S. Larsen, Tron Omland, Henrikke G. Rustad

item.title: Height growth of rational self-maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.33570v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field or a function field of a curve. Let $f$ be a dominant rational self-map of a normal projective variety $X$ of dimension $d$ over $K$, and let $h_H\geq1$ be an ample Weil height. Let $\lambda_1(f)$ denote the first dynamical degree of $f$. We show that there is a constant $C_{f,h_H}>0$ such that, for any $n\geq1$ and any point $P\in X(\overline{K})$ with well-defined forward orbit, $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2(d-1)}\lambda_1(f)^n$ if $\lambda_1(f)>1$, and $h_H(f^n(P))\leq C_{f,h_H}h_H(P)n^{2d}$ if $\lambda_1(f)=1$. Over number fields, the proof combines a new uniform upper bound for arithmetic degrees with a uniform comparison of point heights. Over function fields, it relies on the corresponding uniform upper bound for geometric degrees on a projective model.
item.dc:creator: Fei Hu, Jiarui Song

item.title: Improved Global Boundedness Criteria via Refined Bootstrap Estimates for a Quasilinear Chemotaxis-May-Nowak System
item.description: arXiv:2610.33657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a quasilinear chemotaxis--May--Nowak system with nonlinear diffusion growing at least as $s^{m-1}$ at high densities and derive improved criteria for global existence and uniform boundedness. For the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic system, we establish global boundedness when $m>3-\frac{4}{n}$ for $n\in\{2,3\}$ and when $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. For the fully parabolic system, the same conclusion holds under $m>1+\frac{n}{4}$ for $n\ge4$. The proof relies on two refined estimates. Weighted space--time control of the nonlinear infection source yields the low-order $L^q$-bounds for the free virus density needed to initiate the bootstrap in the parabolic--elliptic--parabolic case. Subsequently, preserving the product structure of this source in the interpolation argument allows the chemotactic contribution to be absorbed more efficiently by the nonlinear diffusion. These estimates improve the previously known sufficient conditions for global boundedness.
item.dc:creator: Xueli Bai, Fang Li, Suying Liu, Xuxuan Luo

item.title: Global invertibility of polynomial mappings and connectedness of preimages of large spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.33875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a polynomial mapping $\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ with nowhere zero Jacobian determinant is a global diffeomorphism provided the preimage of large circles are connected. In higher dimensions this result fails and we present families of counterexamples. Yet, in dimension $3$, we prove that if the preimages of large spheres are connected, then the Jelonek set of the mapping is not homeomorphic to a line and, provided that it has codimension at least $2$, cannot have a single end at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Francisco Braun, Zbigniew Jelonek, Maria Michalska

item.title: The measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups
item.description:
arXiv:2610.34323v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article we show that all the nonamenable Baumslag-Solitar groups with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree, i.e., $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ with $|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p|
eq |q|$, are measure equivalent to each other, thereby completing the measure equivalence classification of Baumslag-Solitar groups: each $\mathrm{BS}(p,q)$ belongs to one of three measure equivalence classes according to whether it is amenable ($|p|=1$ or $|q|=1$), virtually isomorphic to $\mathbf{F}_n 	imes \mathbf{Z}$ ($|p|=|q|
eq 1$), or is nonamenable with nonunimodular Bass-Serre tree ($|p|,|q| 
eq 1$ and $|p| 
eq |q|$). More generally, we obtain the similar classification of the generalized Baumslag-Solitar groups of rank $1$ (i.e., groups that act cocompactly on a tree with edge and vertex stabilizers infinite cyclic). Our proof also establishes a classification of all treeable lcsc groups into exactly six measure equivalence classes. Our new contribution which completes this taxonomy is: all nonunimodular nonamenable treeable lcsc groups are measure equivalent. Along the way we obtain several results about type $\mathrm{III}$ equivalence relations and graphings of independent interest. For example, we show that every ergodic type $\mathrm{III}_0$ graphing admits an ergodic hyperfinite subgraph for which the natural factor map of Krieger flows is an isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Damien Gaboriau, Antoine Poulin, Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob, Konrad Wr\'obel

item.title: Extrapolating learned dynamics across bifurcations based on generalized synchronization
item.description: arXiv:2610.34471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Predicting dynamics across bifurcations by extrapolating trained models is crucial in diverse fields of physics. Generalized synchronization provides a framework for understanding dynamical reconstruction by neural networks, especially in the context of reservoir computing. Building on this framework, we derive a formula combining pretrained readouts to reconstruct unseen chaotic dynamics. Using classical Lagrange interpolation theory, we derive rigorous bounds on readout errors and conjugacy residuals. Numerical examples demonstrate accurate prediction of chaotic dynamics across bifurcations.
item.dc:creator: Lingfeng Chen, Masanobu Inubushi

item.title: Dynamical Chowla conjecture for polynomials of several variables
item.description: arXiv:2610.34912v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the mean value of the Liouville function at non-square one-variable polynomials is zero. This conjecture is a generalization of the prime number theorem (PNT). In 2022, Bergelson and Richter established a dynamical generalization of this form of the PNT. For non-square multivariate polynomials, one also expects that Chowla's conjecture is true. In this article, we extend Bergelson and Richter's result to multivariate polynomials whose Birch rank is sufficiently large in terms of their degree. We also establish analogous results for averages over integer points on algebraic varieties.
item.dc:creator: Biao Wang, Daodao Yang

item.title: Modular Existential Closedness
item.description: arXiv:2610.35409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the Modular Existential Closedness conjecture for the modular $j$-function extended from the upper half-plane to $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$ by Schwarz reflection. Specifically, we show that any system of equations involving the field operations and $j$ has solutions in the complex numbers unless it is overdetermined. Such a system is overdetermined if, roughly, there are more independent equations than variables, possibly after applying the transformation rules of the $j$-function under the linear fractional action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q})$ on $\mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. In general, we do not expect overdetermined systems of equations to have solutions due to the algebraic and transcendental properties of the $j$-function captured by the modular analogue of Schanuel's conjecture. In geometric terms, Modular Existential Closedness states that given a broad and free irreducible algebraic variety $V \subseteq \mathbb{C}^n \times \mathbb{C}^n$ -- where broadness and freeness are geometric conditions guaranteeing that the system is not overdetermined -- there is a point of the form $(\tau_1, \ldots, \tau_n, j(\tau_1), \ldots, j(\tau_n)) \in V$ with $\tau_i \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \mathbb{R}$. The proof uses Ratner's theorems on the closure and equidistribution of the orbits of unipotent flows in powers of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ to describe the asymptotic behaviour of the orbits of certain analytic maps. This is then applied to approximate a relatively simple system of equations using the original system and the action of $\rm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$. The construction of the limiting system makes use of the Ax--Schanuel theorem and guarantees an isolated solution. Rouch\'e's theorem then establishes the existence of solutions for the original system of equations.
item.dc:creator: Vahagn Aslanyan

item.title: Finite-step projective dynamics of Schr\"odinger cocycles: non-degeneracy, regularity, and rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2610.35583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the no deterministic images condition (NDI) for Schr\"odinger cocycles, which excludes a common image of a fixed probability measure under almost all projective transfer transformations. We prove two-step NDI at every energy for nonconstant measurable potentials over mixing systems and ergodic potentials with infinite essential range, and classify persistence for finite-state locally constant potentials. For bounded Markov and hidden Markov potentials on general state spaces under a one-step $L^2$ norm gap condition on the Markov operator, we prove H\"older bounds for solution-direction distributions above an exponential cutoff and H\"older conditional stationary measures. Counterexamples show the essential sharpness of both assumptions. For nonconstant real trigonometric potentials, including the almost Mathieu operator, we prove NDI and H\"older bounds for distributions of solution directions at all steps $k\ge2$ and all frequencies (rational or irrational). The exponent depends on the step, while the constant is uniform in steps, frequency and energy on compact intervals. For every irrational frequency and every energy with positive Lyapunov exponent, we prove non-atomicity of both Oseledets direction distributions and convergence to the unstable distribution from every phase-independent initial probability. This gives a new criterion for a zero Lyapunov exponent: a subsequential limit with an atom for one fixed initial direction suffices. All these results extend to an analytic class, with step-dependent regularity bounds.
item.dc:creator: Mira Shamis

item.title: Phase response approach to networked neural activity models with delays
item.description: arXiv:2610.35638v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Networks of delay-coupled neural mass models alternate between synchrony and anti-phase locking as the delay between brain regions increases. The origin of these delay-dependent bands has remained unclear. Here, we show that a single function, the phase interaction function $H$ of an isolated node, predicts where the bands occur and explains why they repeat. For a Wilson--Cowan model with intra-nodal delay $\tau$ and inter-nodal delay $\rho$, we compute the limit cycle and phase response, and hence $H$, by harmonic balance. Each band boundary is a zero of $H'$ shifted by the phase lag $\Omega\rho$, so the bands repeat in $\rho$ with the oscillation period. Simulations of the full delay-differential networks confirm these predictions, from two nodes, where predicted frequencies agree to second order in the coupling strength, to rings, where the theory also identifies coexisting stable twisted states that random initial conditions rarely reach. At weak coupling, the delays at which synchrony gains or loses stability are set by the node dynamics alone, whereas stable anti-phase states require a bipartite network. For a macaque connectome, metastability peaks at the edges of the synchrony bands, where the stability margin of phase-locking vanishes. The reduction is accurate for coupling strengths well below the slowest Floquet exponent of the node, beyond which a phase--amplitude description is needed. More broadly, vanishing phase-locking stability provides a simple route to metastability in delay-coupled oscillator networks and a candidate mechanism for the flexible coordination of brain dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Martin R Nelson, Jonathan J Crofts

item.title: Topological Pressure of Discontinuous Potentials and Variational Principle for Flows
item.description: arXiv:2403.15753v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a compact metric space and $\Phi=\{\varphi_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ be a continuous flow on $X$. We introduce two types of topological pressure for family of discontinuous potentials $a=\{a_t\}_{t>0}$. First, define the topological pressure of family of measurable potentials $a=\{a_t\}_{t>0}$ on a subset $Z$ for flow and proof its invariant principle. The second topological pressure is defined on a invariant subset having a nested family of subsets, we also proof its invariant principle.
item.dc:creator: Ruolan Xiong Yunhua Zhou

item.title: Tropical thermodynamic formalism
item.description: arXiv:2408.10169v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the zero-temperature large deviation principle for equilibrium states in the context of distance-expanding maps. The logarithmic-type zero-temperature limit in the large deviation principle induces a tropical algebra structure, which motivates our study of the tropical adjoint Bousch operator $\mathcal{L}_A^{*}$ since the Bousch operator $\mathcal{L}_A$ is tropical linear and corresponds to the Ruelle operator $\mathcal{R}_A$. We extend tropical functional analysis, define the adjoint operator $\mathcal{L}_A^{*}$ as a tropical analog of the adjoint Ruelle operator $\mathcal{R}_A^{*}$, and establish the existence and generic uniqueness of tropical eigendensities of $\mathcal{L}_A^{*}$ associated with the maximal eigenvalue. The Aubry set and the Ma\~{n}\'{e} potential, both originating from weak KAM theory, serve as important tools in the representations of tropical eigendensities. With our notion of tropical completeness and our tropical Riesz representation theorem, $\mathcal{L}_A^{*}$ can also be seen as a version of the tropical Koopman operator.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqiang Li, Yiqing Sun

item.title: Historical behavior of skew products and arcsine laws
item.description: arXiv:2501.00266v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the occurrence of historical behavior for almost every point in the setting of skew products with one-dimensional fiber dynamics. Under suitable ergodic conditions, we establish that a weak form of the arcsine law leads to the non-convergence of Birkhoff averages along almost every orbit. As an application, we show that this phenomenon occurs for one-step skew product maps over a Bernoulli shift, where the stochastic process induced by the iterates of the fiber maps is conjugate to a random walk. Furthermore, we revisit known examples of skew products that exhibit historical behavior almost everywhere, verifying that they fulfill the required ergodic and probabilistic conditions. Consequently, our results provide a unified and generalized framework that connects such behaviors to the arcsine distribution of the orbits.
item.dc:creator: Pablo G. Barrientos, Raul R. Chavez

item.title: On the closure of irregular orbits of the horocyclic flow on infinite finness
item.description: arXiv:2504.20274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The topological dynamics of the horocyclic flow h_R on the unit tangent bundle of a geometrically finite hyperbolic surface is well known. In particular on such a surface the flow h_R is minimal or the minimal sets are the periodic orbits. When the surface is geometrically infinite, the situation is more complex and the presence of possible irregular orbits makes the description of minimal sets complicated. In this text, we construct a family of infinite hyperbolic surfaces for which the horocyclic flow defined on the unit tangent bundle is not minimal.
item.dc:creator: Amadou Sy, Masseye Gaye

item.title: On intertwined polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2510.01877v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be polynomials of degree at least two over $\mathbb C$. We say that $A_1$ and $A_2$ are intertwined if the endomorphism $(A_1, A_2)$ of $\mathbb C\mathbb P^1 \times \mathbb C\mathbb P^1$ given by $(z_1, z_2) \mapsto (A_1(z_1), A_2(z_2))$ admits an irreducible periodic curve that is neither a vertical nor a horizontal line. For a polynomial $A$, we denote by $\mathrm{Inter}(A)$ the set of all polynomials $B$ such that some iterate of $B$ is intertwined with some iterate of $A$. In this paper, we prove a conjecture of Favre and Gauthier describing the structure of $\mathrm{Inter}(A)$. We also obtain a sharp bound on the periods of periodic curves for endomorphisms $(A_1, A_2)$ in terms of the sizes of the symmetry groups of the Julia sets of $A_1$ and $A_2$.
item.dc:creator: Fedor Pakovich

item.title: The Radon--Nikodym topography of acyclic measured graphs
item.description: arXiv:2512.24741v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The classical Adams dichotomy [Ada90] characterizes amenability of probability-measure-preserving treed equivalence relations in terms of the ends of a given treeing. We extend this dichotomy to the measure-class-preserving (mcp) setting by analyzing the Radon--Nikodym topography of an acyclic mcp Borel graph, i.e., the interaction between the graph geometry and the associated Radon--Nikodym cocycle. In the general mcp setting one must count not all ends, but only the nonvanishing ends: those ends which have positive upper cocycle-weight. More precisely, we prove that a locally countable acyclic mcp graph is amenable if and only if a.e. component has at most two nonvanishing ends, while it is nowhere amenable exactly when a.e. component has a nonempty perfect closed set of nonvanishing ends. At the heart of our analysis lies the study of acyclic countable-to-one Borel functions. Our critical result is that, outside of the essentially two-ended setting, all back ends in a.e. orbit are vanishing and have cocycle-finite geodesics. We also give several characterizations, including topographical and cocycle-free, of essential one-endedness of such functions, and show that the number of barytropic ends controls the essential number of ends. Our proofs utilize mass transport, end selection, and the notion of the Radon--Nikodym core for acyclic mcp graphs, a new concept that serves as a guiding framework for our topographical analysis.
item.dc:creator: Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob

item.title: The extended future cover and desynchronization of sofic shifts
item.description: arXiv:2603.09593v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The paper describes a cover of the future cover of a sofic shift which is canonical in the same way as the future cover itself. In some cases the cover is isomorphic to the future cover and in other it is a genuine extension. The extended future cover is then used to introduce and describe the desynchronization of sofic shifts.
item.dc:creator: Klaus Thomsen

item.title: Neuromorphic Realization of Best Response in Finite-Action Games
item.description: arXiv:2604.03222v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a mechanistic dynamical-systems formulation of best response in finite-action games with relational structure on the action set. The proposed neuromorphic decision dynamics realize best response as the stable outcome of an internal state-space process, rather than as an externally imposed choice rule. This provides a deterministic account of commitment formation, symmetry resolution through basins of attraction, and hysteresis and decision persistence under perturbations. For action spaces with circulant coupling, we prove using Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction that the action-coupling operator determines which components of evidence govern decision formation. We further show that the dynamics implicitly compute a geometry-aware utility, converge exponentially to the corresponding best response, and switch only when evidence is sufficiently strong. In contrast, supplying the same geometry-aware utility directly to logit dynamics does not recover these properties, showing that relational structure must be embedded in the decision mechanism itself. We illustrate the framework in a repeated coverage game, prove that the induced game is an exact potential game, and show that its Nash equilibria are reached by the neuromorphic decision dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Himani Sinhmar, Vaibhav Srivastava, Naomi Ehrich Leonard

item.title: On local solutions to time-varying linear systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.07043v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops an intrinsic framework for local solutions to time-varying linear systems with real meromorphic coefficients. Local solutions on compact intervals naturally form a sheaf of vector spaces. We introduce regularity triples to distinguish regularity across singularities, one-sided regularity at singularities, and regularity away from singularities. The local formulation isolates a continuation property implicit in established global frameworks and yields a simple definition of behavioural controllability. We establish an algebraically verifiable sufficient condition for continuation, prove its necessity for controllability, and derive an algebraic characterization of controllability based on the Teichm\"uller-Nakayama form, recovering and slightly generalizing established results.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Samuel Bock

item.title: WSINDy for Model Predictive Control with Applications to Fusion, Drones, and Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2604.23269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The control of complex dynamical systems remains a fundamental challenge in science and engineering, where strong nonlinearities, the presence of noise, and computational constraints often pose significant obstacles in traditional control approaches. Recent advances in data-driven methods, particularly system identification techniques, have shown a powerful alternative by providing fast, parsimonious, interpretable models that are well-suited for model predictive control (MPC). Building on these developments, the present article embeds WSINDy with actuation inputs (WSINDYc) within a MPC framework. Compared to benchmark data-driven methods, WSINDYc enables a more robust identification of the governing dynamics, particularly in the presence of high noise levels, resulting in more accurate and efficient control. The capabilities of the proposed WSINDY-MPC framework are demonstrated on a range of problems, including a tokamak plasma boundary model that includes main ion gas puff actuation, drone tracking and collision avoidance, the chaotic Lorenz system, and a simplified flight control model for an F-8 aircraft. The proposed framework achieves superior performance in the presence of noise, enabling longer prediction horizons, lower trajectory tracking error, and a more reliable obstacle clearance, while simultaneously achieving lower MPC cost values compared to the baseline methods.
item.dc:creator: Cristian L\'opez, Mckenna Partridge, Sebastian De Pascuale, Jeremy Lore, Andrew Christlieb, Stephen Becker, David M. Bortz

item.title: Time-periodic carrying simplex for a competitive system of Carath\'eodory ODEs
item.description: arXiv:2605.01287v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the existence of a time-periodic carrying simplex for competitive systems of Kolmogorov-type ordinary differential equations of the form $\dot{x}_i = x_i g_i(t,x)$, $i=1,\dots,d$, on $\mathbb{R}^d_+$, where the vector field $g$ is $T$-periodic in time and satisfies only Carath\'eodory conditions rather than the classical $C^1$ regularity assumed in earlier work. We show that the time-$T$ Poincar\'e map $P$ generated by the flow is retrotone, and apply recent results on the carrying simplex for retrotone maps to obtain for $P$ a carrying simplex $\Sigma$ that is an unordered, Lipschitz, invariant manifold homeomorphic to the standard probability simplex, and that attracts all nonzero trajectories of the discrete dynamical system generated by $P$. We then extend this construction to the full nonautonomous flow by introducing an auxiliary autonomous system on the extended phase space $\mathcal{T} \times \mathbb{R}^d_+$, where $\mathcal{T}$ is the circle of length $T$, generated via a skew-product formulation. In the context of this extended phase space we then construct a compact global attractor and identify, as its relative boundary, a time-periodic family of carrying simplices $\{\Sigma_s\}_{s \in \mathcal{T}}$ that depend continuously on the phase $s$, each homeomorphic to the standard simplex and each attracting, uniformly in $s$, all nonzero orbits of the corresponding time-shifted flow. These results provide a rigorous foundation for the qualitative analysis of seasonally forced competitive population models in which growth rates need only be measurable and locally Lipschitz in time, broadening the applicability of carrying simplex theory to more realistic ecological settings.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Dynamics and Differential Equations, 2026
item.dc:creator: Stephen Baigent, Janusz Mierczy\'nski

item.title: Degree growth, orbit graphs, and functoriality for birational dynamical systems
item.description: arXiv:2606.29274v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to give a natural divisor-theoretic formulation of the counting method introduced by Halburd for computing degree growth, in a form applicable to birational dynamical systems on varieties of arbitrary dimension. Instead of counting only preimages of special values, we follow time-indexed divisorial conditions through singularity patterns. These conditions are recorded on normalized finite-window orbit graphs, where the relevant multiplicities are realized as divisorial valuations of pullbacks of time-indexed divisors. This construction explains how the elementary computations appearing in singularity patterns can be interpreted as degree relations on a single normal variety. We then show that further relations arise from the failure of functoriality of pullbacks: when the center of a divisor enters the relevant indeterminacy locus, a degree-drop divisor appears. Under suitable finite-type assumptions, the two kinds of relations lead to closed linear difference systems governing degree sequences. Several examples, including higher-dimensional ones, demonstrate that the two mechanisms are complementary and that their combination determines the degree growth in cases where either mechanism alone is insufficient.
item.dc:creator: Tomoyuki Takenawa

item.title: Entropy Scales in Topological Dynamical Systems
item.description: arXiv:2608.10460v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we define topological and measure-theoretic entropy scales in dynamical systems for the scaling introduced by Helfter. Firstly, we establish a variational principle between Bowen and lower entropy scales on compact subsets. Secondly, we prove factor inequalities for Bowen and upper capacity entropy scales on arbitrary subsets; unlike the classical additive case, the fiber contribution is described by a transfer function and need not be additive. We also study entropy scales and sequence entropy scales under the induced action. Under suitable conditions, zero values are preserved in both directions, while positive values become infinite; counterexamples show that additional assumptions are generally necessary. As an application, we use entropy scales to distinguish zero-entropy systems sharing the same entropy dimension but differ in finer orbit-growth rates.
item.dc:creator: Yunxiang Xie, Ercai Chen, Xiaoyao Zhou

item.title: On The Spectral Properties of Discrete Landscape Functions
item.description: arXiv:2608.11372v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the landscape function on a discretized interval. The discrete landscape has an explicit closed form, and its spectral coefficients can be computed exactly. We show that these coefficients lie in explicit abelian extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ and obtain the bound $$[\mathbb{Q}(c_k(N)):\mathbb{Q}]\leq\varphi(N)$$ for every odd $k$. The Chandra--Jain conjecture, asserting that $[\mathbb{Q}(c_1(N)):\mathbb{Q}]=\varphi(N)$ for all $N\geq3$, has since been proved by Q. Zhou (Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21935814). We then reduce higher modes to the coprime case. Exact computations for all 624 pairs with $3\leq N\leq50$ reveal only the degrees $\varphi(N/d)$ and $2\varphi(N/d)$ for non-coprime modes, where $d=\gcd(N,k)$. This motivates the Second Chandra--Jain Conjecture that this degree dichotomy holds generally. We also discuss connections with parity, the Arnold cat map, and Lefschetz numbers.
item.dc:creator: Aryaman Chandra, S. R. Jain

item.title: A Lean~4 Framework for the Radii Polynomial Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.02335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Computer-assisted proofs in dynamics establish results about nonlinear systems by rigorous numerical computation. Their correctness rests on a trusted base of interval-arithmetic libraries and analytic estimates checked by hand. We formalize in Lean~4 a framework for the radii polynomial method, which certifies an exact solution near a numerical approximation by verifying four norm bounds and the resulting polynomial inequality. Weighted coefficient algebras provide the common setting for polynomial equations and initial value problems in Taylor and Chebyshev series. Their universal properties construct the bounded operators and the evaluation maps, and the universal property of the free commutative algebra makes polynomial substitution commute with evaluation. Finite/tail reductions turn the four norm bounds into finite rational inequalities, which are checked in Lean. The radii theorem then yields an exact coefficient solution, and realization theorems carry it to a solution of the original equation. The worked examples are a square-root branch given by a convergent power series and polynomial initial value problems, among them the Lorenz system, for which the library proves existence, uniqueness within the trajectory ball, and analyticity of the function-level solution.
item.dc:creator: Fengyang Wang, Konstantin Mischaikow, Marcio Gameiro

item.title: Beta-shifts without typical periodic optimization
item.description: arXiv:2610.03619v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that beta-shifts whose lexicographically largest point is a Sturmian sequence do not have typical periodic optimization (TPO): on each such beta-shift there is a non-empty open set of Lipschitz functions whose unique maximizing measure is the Sturmian measure, which is not supported on a periodic orbit. These are the first known examples of beta-shifts without TPO, and, since they have the specification property, the first known examples of shift spaces with specification but without TPO. The corresponding beta-transformations do not have TPO in any space of H\"older functions on the interval. The main ingredient in the proofs is a rigidity property of Sturmian subshifts: modulo constants and Lipschitz coboundaries, the space of Lipschitz functions on such a subshift is one-dimensional. We also show that the set of $\beta>1$ for which the beta-shift or the beta-transformation does not have TPO is dense in $(1,\infty)$, but has zero packing dimension. The density is proved by a tuning construction, analogous to Douady--Hubbard tuning in the Mandelbrot set, which produces non-Sturmian subshifts with the same rigidity property. Finally, we show that every beta-shift has typical zero-entropy optimization: for an open dense set of Lipschitz functions, the maximizing measure is unique and its support has zero topological entropy.
item.dc:creator: Wen Huang, Oliver Jenkinson, Leiye Xu, Yiwei Zhang

item.title: Symmetry-breaking in a discrete-choice LQG mean field game
item.description: arXiv:2610.05730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Mean-field games provide a continuum framework for modeling the dynamics of large, interacting populations of non-cooperative agents. This paper studies symmetry-breaking in a finite-horizon, two-choice min-LQG mean-field game in which identical agents with linear stochastic dynamics choose one of two equally desirable terminal destinations, while trading off control effort against social pressure to conform. The model has an odd symmetry between the two destinations and therefore always admits a symmetric, dynamic Nash equilibrium in which the population splits evenly between them, producing a deadlock collective state at final time. Numerical studies have suggested that, as the penalty for social nonconformity increases, this symmetric equilibrium loses stability as a fixed point of an associated scalar, self-consistency map, and asymmetric consensus Nash equilibria emerge, where most agents select the same destination. By analyzing the linearized forward-backward PDE system through the scalar map representation, we provide a proof of this loss of stability of the symmetric equilibrium. Together with the odd symmetry of the map, this implies the existence of symmetry-broken mean-field game equilibria corresponding to consensus on either destination.
item.dc:creator: Ali Akbar Rezaei Lori, Piyush Grover

item.title: Existence and Uniqueness Proof for the Transport Equation and the Orthogonal Dynamics Equation for Zwanzig's Projection on Gaussian Spaces: A Vanishing Viscosity Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.18647v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the existence of unique solutions ${u\in H^1(0,T;L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))}$ of the transport equation $u_t=F\cdot\nabla u+f$ and the orthogonal dynamics equation ${u_t= Q_\text{Z} (F\cdot\nabla) Q_\text{Z} u+f}$, where $F$ is a time-independent vector field, $f$ is a forcing term, $P_\text{Z}=1-Q_\text{Z}$ is a Zwanzig projection (conditional expectation) on $L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)$ defined by $P_\text{Z}h \propto \int h(\cdot ,y) \rho(\cdot,y)\rm{d}y$, and $\gamma$ is the standard Gaussian measure with density $\rho$. To this end, we develop a vanishing viscosity method based on the maximal regularity theory for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator on $L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)$. The following assumptions guarantee the existence and uniqueness of strong solutions: ${f\in H^1(0,T;L^2_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))\cap L^2(0,T;H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n))}$, ${g\in H^1_\gamma(\mathbb{R}^n)}$, $F\in W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $\rm{ess\,sup}_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(x\cdot F-\rm{div}F\right) < \infty$, where $g$ denotes the initial value function.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Widder

item.title: Pointwise convergence of bilinear ergodic averages for commuting transformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26388v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $S,Q:X\to X$ be commuting probability-preserving transformations. Let $1\leq p,q\leq\infty$ satisfy $1/p+1/q\leq1$. We prove that, for every fixed $F\in L^p(\mu)$ and $G\in L^q(\mu)$, the averages $$ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N F(S^nx)G(Q^nx) $$ converge almost everywhere as $N\to\infty$. Our proof introduces a new analytic approach that relies on neither the circle method nor characteristic-factor theory. Exploiting the triangular structure arising from commuting transformations, we combine matrix-energy estimates with Gaussian heat-flow arguments to establish pointwise variation inequalities for suitable smooth averages. We then use even and odd Gaussian kernels to recover the convergence of the original averages.
item.dc:creator: Zhuowen Guo, Rongzhong Xiao, Shuhao Zhang

item.title: Measures of maximal entropy for meromorphic maps on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28617v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f$ be a dominant meromorphic self-map of a compact K\"ahler manifold. Assume that $f$ has a strictly dominant intermediate dynamical degree $\lambda$ and that the number of isolated $n$-periodic points, counted with multiplicity, is at most $\lambda^n+o(\lambda^n)$. Then $f$ admits at most one adapted invariant probability measure of entropy $\log\lambda$.
