If such a measure exists, its natural extension is Bernoulli, and the isolated periodic points equidistribute towards it when counted with or without multiplicity. We apply this criterion to several classes of maps in complex dynamics, resolving longstanding open problems.
item.dc:creator: Muhan Luo, Qi Zhou

item.title: New criteria for upper bounds on the number of limit cycles in Li\'enard systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.30417v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish criteria for at most one or at most two limit cycles of generalized Li\'enard systems in a single potential well. Two independent uniqueness tests use modified quotients of the damping and restoring forces; both allow a degenerate restoring force, and one extends to continuous potential profiles with corners. Opposite convexity of the two branches of the damping quotient in the potential coordinate gives an upper bound of two. Further criteria apply to weak damping with an analytic normalized profile on a bounded potential interval under an explicit smallness condition, to small profile perturbations vanishing near the equilibrium on a bounded range of half-widths, and to parameter families satisfying curvature, monotonicity and boundary conditions. Applications give another proof of the classical quartic bound. For Selkov systems, we obtain a two-cycle bound in a specified negative-parameter region and prove existence and uniqueness in a positive-parameter region. We also prove Conjecture~2.1 in [J. Math. Anal. Appl., 2025]. Examples attain the two-cycle bound.
item.dc:creator: Chen Cao, Hebai Chen, Yilei Tang

item.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
item.description: arXiv:2610.32820v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures satisfying Pesin's entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms whose attractors admit extendable continuous invariant splittings. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with strictly separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. We also construct examples with hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Bai, Wanshan Lin, Xueting Tian

item.title: Arbitrarily Many Primitive Prime Divisors in an Iterate of $x^d+c$
item.description: arXiv:2209.07624v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field with ring of integers $R$, let $f_{d,c}(x)=x^d+c\in K[x]$ be a unicritical polynomial of degree $d\ge2$, and let $\varrho_d(n,c)$ denote the number of primitive prime divisors of $f_{d,c}^n(0)$, the $n$-th term of the critical orbit of $f_{d,c}$. We show that $\varrho_d(n,c)$ admits no uniform bound, that is, no bound depending only on $d$ and $n$. More precisely, for all $n\ge1$ and $t\ge1$ there is $c\in R$ for which $f_{d,c}^n(0)$ has at least $t$ primitive prime divisors, and these primes may be prescribed to occur with any given multiplicities. This can be done simultaneously for any finite set of iterates. The construction rests on a density computation. Namely, the set of primes occurring as a primitive prime divisor of $f_{d,c}^n(0)$ for some $c$ has positive density. We compute that density explicitly for $d=2$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, under a hypothesis on the Galois group of the associated Gleason polynomial, verified for $n\le16$. As an application, we produce, for every $m\ge1$, a parameter $c\in R$ (in fact, a whole residue class of them), for which the splitting field of $f_{d,c}^m(x)$ has the maximal possible degree over $K$.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Sadek, Mohamed Wafik

item.title: Convergence of Quantum Lindstedt Series and Semiclassical Renormalization
item.description: arXiv:2301.12728v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work we consider the KAM renormalizability problem for small pseudodifferential perturbations of the semiclassical isochronous transport operator with Diophantine frequencies on the torus. Assuming that the symbol of the perturbation is real analytic and globally bounded, we prove convergence of the quantum Lindstedt series and describe completely the set of semiclassical measures and quantum limits of the renormalized system. Each of these measures is given by symplectic deformation of the Haar measure on an invariant torus for the unperturbed classical system.
item.dc:creator: Victor Arnaiz

item.title: Comparing Periodic Point Invariants for Parameterized Families of Maps
item.description: arXiv:2508.18339v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compare different periodic point invariants for families of maps parameterized over a compact manifold. Malkiewich and Ponto showed that, in the case of a single map, the Fuller trace is equivalent to the collection of Reidmeister traces of iterates. In this paper, we show that, in contrast to the case of a single map, the fiberwise Fuller trace is a strictly more sensitive invariant than the collection of fiberwise Reidemeister traces of iterates. This resolves a conjecture of Malkiewich and Ponto. We also prove that our construction gives a geometric representation of elements of the kernel of the ghost map out of topological restriction homology.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Williams

item.title: Lubin's conjecture for height-one $p$-adic dynamical systems over $p(p-1)$-tame extensions
item.description: arXiv:2603.03873v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove Lubin's conjecture for height-one commuting pairs of formal power series defined over the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}$ of finite extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$ whose ramification index is coprime to $p(p-1)$. For such a pair $(f, u)$, with $f$ noninvertible and $u$ invertible, we show that $(f, u)$ is a pair of endomorphisms of a formal group defined over $\mathcal{O}$. The proof relies on extracting a crystalline character of weight $1$ from the Galois set $T_f$ of $f$-consistent sequences, using it to define a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-module structure on $T_f$ for which $f$ is an endomorphism, and applying explicit functors in integral $p$-adic Hodge theory to recover the latent formal group.
item.dc:creator: Martin Debaisieux

item.title: Optimality and annealing path planning of dynamical analog solvers
item.description: arXiv:2603.13778v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently proposed analog solvers based on dynamical systems, such as Ising machines, are promising platforms for large-scale combinatorial optimization. Yet, given the heuristic nature of the field, there is very limited insight on optimality guarantees of the solvers, as well as how parameter schedules shape dynamics and outcomes. Here, we develop a dynamical mean-field framework to analyze Ising-machine dynamics for finding the ground state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick(SK) model of spin glasses and identify mechanisms that enable rapid convergence to provenly near-optimal energies. For a fixed target energy density Ec, we show that solutions are typically reached within O(1) matrix vector multiplications, indicating constant time complexity. We further delineate theoretical limitations arising from different parameter-scheduling trajectories and demonstrate a pronounced benefit of temperature-only annealing for the Coherent Ising Machine. Building on these insights, we propose a general framework for designing optimized parameter schedules, thereby improving the practical effectiveness of Ising machines for complex optimization tasks. The superior performance of the dynamical solvers is illustrated by the attainment of the ground state energy of the SK model.
item.dc:creator: Shu Zhou, K. Y. Michael Wong, Juntao Wang, David Shui Wing Hui, Daniel Ebler, Jie Sun

item.title: Formulation and Learning Of The Forecasting Problem
item.description: arXiv:2603.20359v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Machine learning has opened new frontiers in purely data-driven forecasting of dynamical systems; the resulting methods are showing considerable promise in some application domains. However, in contrast to model-driven algorithms, analysis of these data-driven methods is poorly developed. In this paper we address this issue, developing a theory to underpin data-driven methods to solve forecasting problems. The theoretical framework comprises two key components: (i) establishing the existence of a mapping defining the forecasting problem; (ii) showing that it is possible to approximate this mapping by supervised learning techniques, to arbitrary accuracy. We work in the continuous-time and noise-free setting as this defines a simple canonical setting in which to establish an underpinning theory; the continuous-time setting leads to an operator formulation of the problem in which the underlying forecasting map is defined on pathspace. As a byproduct of our framework we show that analogous existence and approximation results may be obtained for the smoothing problem of recovering unobserved components of dynamical systems, from observed components, using supervised learning. The theoretical results, for both forecasting and smoothing, are illustrated with experiments studying the Lorenz `63, Lorenz `96 and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Edoardo Calvello, Elizabeth Carlson, Nikola Kovachki, Michael N. Manta, Andrew M. Stuart

item.title: Canonical separating coordinates in the generalized cubic H\'enon-Heiles systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.19188v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the three classical integrable generalized cubic H\'enon--Heiles systems -- Kaup--Kupershmidt, KdV$_5$, and Sawada--Kotera -- from the viewpoint of bi-Hamiltonian geometry and separation of variables. On the standard symplectic manifold $T^*\mathbb R^2$, we construct compatible Poisson deformations $P_1=L_XP_0$, compute the associated recursion operators $N=P_1P_0^{-1}$, and analyze the action of $N^*$ on the codistribution generated by the first integrals. This yields the corresponding control matrices, whose eigenvalues provide the separating coordinates. For the generalized Kaup--Kupershmidt case we carry out the construction explicitly: we determine a deformation vector field, the compatible Poisson tensor, the torsionless recursion operator, the control matrix, the separating coordinates, and, crucially, the conjugate momenta. We then derive the separated relations and write the Hamilton equations in canonical separated variables, thus decomposing the original Hamiltonian system into two separated subsystems. To the best of our knowledge, this explicit derivation of the separating variables and, in particular, of the conjugate momenta for the generalized Kaup--Kupershmidt system is new. For the KdV$_5$ and Sawada--Kotera cases we show how the same bi-Hamiltonian scheme applies, emphasizing both the common geometric mechanism and the features peculiar to each system. In this way, the three generalized cubic H\'enon--Heiles systems are treated within a unified framework based on compatible Poisson structures, recursion operators, control matrices, and Darboux--Nijenhuis coordinates.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Portaluri, Nicola Sottocornola

item.title: $T$-admissible processes and noncommutative weighted ergodic theorems
item.description: arXiv:2604.26224v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we study the bilaterally almost uniform (b.a.u.) convergence of weighted averages of a positive Dunford-Schwartz operator $T$ acting on the noncommutative $L_p$-spaces $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ associated to a semifinite von Neumann algebra $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ for every $1\leq p<\infty$ for a variety of sequences which includes those generated by bounded i.i.d. sequences, the M\"{o}bius function, the Liouville function, and totally balanced automatic sequences. If $1<p<\infty$, then sequences generated by i.i.d. sequences with finite $q$-th moment for $q=\frac{p}{p-1}$ being the H\"{o}lder conjugate of $p$ are also shown to generate good weights for $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We also study similar problems for $T$-admissible processes on a semifinite von Neumann algebra, showing that if a Wiener-Wintner type ergodic theorem holds for a class $\mathcal{W}\subset W_q$ of weights, then it also holds for strongly $p$-bounded $T$-admissible processes assuming that the duality $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$ holds and that $T$ is a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism. A version of this result for arbitrary positive Dunford-Schwartz operators is also considered.
item.dc:creator: Morgan O'Brien

item.title: SpectONet: A Physics-Guided Spectral Deep Operator Network for Euler-Bernoulli Beam Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.25790v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper proposes a novel physics-guided spectral deep operator network, termed SpectONet, for solving Euler-Bernoulli beam (EBB) vibration problems. The proposed framework integrates the operator-learning capability of DeepONet with physics-informed constraints and Chebyshev-Gauss-Lobatto (CGL) sensor placement. Unlike conventional DeepONet frameworks, which commonly employ uniformly distributed sensors, SpectONet uses nonuniform spectral sensor locations with a higher concentration of points near the domain boundaries. This sampling strategy improves the finite-dimensional representation of boundary-sensitive structural responses while requiring only a limited number of branch-network inputs. The governing beam equation, together with the associated initial and boundary conditions, is incorporated into the training objective to promote physically consistent and generalizable predictions. Numerical experiments on three EBB vibration problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Comparisons with strong baseline models such as Vanilla DeepONet, PI-DeepONet, PINN, and CNN-UNet show that SpectONet consistently achieves lower prediction errors across all considered evaluation metrics. In particular, SpectONet achieves an average reduction of approximately 79% in the mean relative $\mathcal{L}_2$ error compared with the best-performing baseline across the three benchmark problems. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of SpectONet as an accurate physics-guided operator-learning framework for structural vibration analysis.
item.dc:creator: Shivani Saini, Ramesh Kumar Vats, Arup Kumar Sahoo

item.title: Two averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2608.16108v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $\lambda$ be the Liouville function. In 1965, Chowla gave a conjecture that the values of $\lambda(n+h_1),\dots, \lambda(n+h_k)$ are asymptotically unrelated for any distinct natural numbers $h_1, \dots, h_k$. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will show a dynamical generalization of Chowla's conjecture on average. In the proof, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. Moreover, we will use this approach to show an analogue of the dynamical Chowla's conjecture along the primes on average. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and a variant for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.
item.dc:creator: Biao Wang

item.title: A characterization of the reversibility of linear cellular automata
item.description: arXiv:2608.20600v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a group, let $\mathbb{K}$ be a field, and let $V$ be a $\mathbb{K}$-vector space. We prove that there exists a bijective linear cellular automaton $V^G\to V^G$ whose inverse is not a cellular automaton if and only if $G$ is not locally finite and $\dim_{\mathbb{K}}V \geq |\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$. In particular, $|\mathbb{K}|^{\aleph_0}$ is the exact dimension threshold for non-reversibility. This answers an open problem proposed by T. Ceccherini-Silberstein and M. Coornaert.
item.dc:creator: Alonso Castillo-Ramirez

item.title: Averaged dynamical generalizations of Chowla's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.14492v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the signs of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at any fixed collection of distinct shifts. In 2015, Matom\"aki, Radziwi\l\l and Tao proved an averaged form of Chowla's conjecture. In 2022, Lichtman proved a variant of this conjecture over primes on average. In the same year, Lichtman and Ter\"av\"ainen proved the Hardy-Littlewood-Chowla conjecture on average. In this article, motivated by the recent work of Bergelson and Richter on the dynamical generalizations of the prime number theorem, we will first establish the analogous dynamical generalizations of these three results related to Chowla's conjecture. In the proofs, we follow an approach of Qi and Zheng who established a variant of Bergelson and Richter's theorem over irreducible binary cubic forms. In 2016, Tao proved that the two-point logarithmic Chowla's conjecture holds. Recently, Charamaras and Richter generalized Tao's theorem to bounded arithmetic functions and proposed a conjecture that generalizes Chowla's conjecture to bounded multi-variable arithmetic functions. Building on their work, we will also prove a dynamical generalization of Tao's theorem and some variants for the composition of the sum-of-digits function with the prime Omega function.
item.dc:creator: Biao Wang, Shaoyun Yi

item.title: Two Answers on Heavy-Ball Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.09912v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We determine the worst-case behavior of the heavy-ball method on smooth strongly convex functions, first for Polyak's quadratic-optimal parameters and then for arbitrary constant parameters. For Polyak's tuning, the exact dimension-uniform exponential rate is the largest growth factor of an interpolable mixture of rotating geometric sequences. Four algebraic families determine this rate at every condition number. Two frequencies suffice, and one function in dimension five attains the rate at every horizon up to constant factors. We recover the sharp convergence threshold $9+4\sqrt5$ of Badithela and Seiler. For general tunings, an exact linear feasibility criterion characterizes dimension-uniform linear convergence through the angle between the characteristic polynomials of the two extreme quadratics. This gives a continuous condition-number threshold and resolves the second heavy-ball riddle of Goujaud, Taylor and Dieuleveut. The regions between consecutive cycle tongues are Farey gaps, each containing convergent and divergent tunings. Regular portions of the threshold surface are analytic plateaus with fixed periodic frequency support. Every rational rotation number in a gap anchors a single-harmonic plateau; mixed-harmonic plateaus and an exact two-lag threshold point also occur. Along tongue edges, explicit multiplier inequalities and second-order expansions of competing Farey fans bound the transition from single-harmonic to mixed-harmonic extremals. The rate bounds and the extremal constructions follow from a common interpolation and separation argument that preserves initialization with zero momentum.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Pasechnyuk-Vilensky, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}
